text:
deploy-bot: rollout v3.0.0 -> 25% traffic. Canary window open (10m). Auto-revert configured: enabled, grace_period=90s. Observed: request error-rate bump on streaming route (p50 ok, p95 higher).

Sam R: saw the alert. Is this systemic or only streaming route?

Jin T: looks streaming-only. Root cause hypothesis: new backpressure handling in stream mux. Gen endpoints unaffected.

Maya S: product note: enterprise customers in APAC are on the streaming route for low-latency features. If we auto-revert, they lose capability mid-contract demo. Can we do a partial pin for those customers?

Priya M: ops: we can pin dedicated pools per customer. That avoids global rollback. We need a quick change to routing rules + update release notes about the degraded streaming path.

Sam R: options: (A) let auto-revert run and restore v2.x globally, (B) manual targeted rollback for streaming route only, (C) override auto-revert and continue rollout while we hotfix. What's the risk tolerance?

Priya M: risk: overriding auto-revert while errors persist may increase surface area. But targeted rollback buys time and keeps rollout for other routes. I'd prefer targeted.

deploy-bot: auto-revert triggered at t+95s due to error-rate threshold. Planned action: rollback v2.9.9 -> revert streaming route. Manual intervention allowed until 1755568050.

Sam R: do NOT let auto-revert do a full global revert. @Priya M proceed with targeted rollback to route streaming for enterprise customer pools back to v2.9.9; leave other routes on v3.0.0.

Priya M: running command to pin pools and adjust routing rules:
```bash
# pin enterprise pools to stable
redwoodctl pool pin --pool enterprise-apac --version v2.9.9 --reason "streaming errors on v3.0.0 canary"
# modify route slice
redwoodctl route update streaming --slice enterprise-apac --version v2.9.9
```

Priya M: done; routing change applied. Verifying traffic now.

Jin T: telemetry shows streaming errors for general users decreased after targeted routing. Canary metrics for other routes stable.

Maya S: marketing/product will send a short note to affected customers; drafting now. Also adding entry to release notes: known issue with stream backpressure handling.

deploy-bot: note 175 - manual changes detected. Auto-revert suspended for global rollout due to manual pin. To force a global revert run: `/deploy rollback v2.9.9 --scope=global --force`

Sam R: log decision here: manual targeted rollback executed to protect enterprise pools; global auto-revert suppressed. Create incident ticket and add action items: quick patch to streaming mux, add streaming smoke test to preflight, and update release notes checklist.

ops-bot: incident created INC-4332. Tagged owners: Jin T (fix), Priya M (routing), Maya S (customer comms).

Priya M: pinned pools verified, no customer impact observed for enterprise demos.

Jin T: starting patch branch: fix/stream-backpressure-guard. Will try hotfix -> canary again after fix. Estimated 45m.

Maya S: I'll post customer comms to #customer-comms once wording approved. Draft: "We noticed a degraded experience on the streaming endpoint for a subset of users after v3.0.0 rollout. We've routed enterprise pools to the previous stable version while we deploy a fix. No action required from customers."

Sam R: approved. Good job team. Final state: streaming route for enterprise pinned to v2.9.9; other routes on v3.0.0; auto-revert suspended globally. We'll reconvene post-hotfix to resume rollout.
